findings.body: The matcher rejects the match when its incorrectly selected characters happen to equal the expected shortcut, and otherwise returns true without checking the grant; tests can pass even when the token has the wrong grant context.

findings.root_cause: The matcher uses the wrong substring bounds and inverts the expected-grant condition.

findings.title: Access-token event tests never verify the expected grant shortcut
findings.trigger: Any event assertion uses isAccessTokenId() with a valid encoded access-token ID such as `onrtac:<uuid>`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 483 in AssertEvents.java shows: if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false. The logic is inverted - it returns false (no match) when the shortcut DOES equal expected, and continues to return true when it doesn't match. Additionally, substring(3,5) extracts chars at indices 3-4, but the comment says 4th char which would be index 3, and the format is 6 chars total (2+2+2) so grant shortcut at positions 4-5 would be substring(4,6).

pr.body:
closes #37118

PR is adding some context information to be available in the `access-token` without a need to introduce any additional custom claims. So far, it provides info about:

- session type (online, offline, transient), which was used to create the token
- token type (regular or lightweight token)
- grant type

These informations can be useful when token is later sent to some Keycloak endpoints (for example introspection, userInfo, admin/account REST API) to optimize something. For example:
- session-type will allow to lookup only correct session type based on the type of the session, which token was created from. As for example today, we need to lookup "online" session and if it is not found, then fallback to "offline" session. So possible unnecessary lookup. Related follow-up issue for optimize that: #37662

- Grant type knowledge can be useful for example for the token-exchange use-case: #37117

- Lightweight access token: We will be able to recognize more reliably if access-token is lightweight or not and do something based on that (EG. lookup roles from model instead of lookup roles from the token)

In this PR, I've made token ID to look something like `onrtac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The first 2 characters is shortcut for "session type" - `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for "token type" - `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for grant type - `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

Shortcuts are used, so the token ID contains important info, but at the same time, it is limited in size and does not introduce much new characters to the token.

The encoding into ID is used only for access-tokens. Not used for refresh tokens or ID tokens or any others.

Introduced dedicated SPI in the end. Wanted to "cache" some objects (EG. shortcuts for grant types etc) and it seems clearer to me to cache them at the level of factory, rather than in the static fields, which is not very pretty. Moreover, provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider (and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc).

#### Note

I've used 2 commits in this PR. Originally, in the 1st commit, I've made the encoding a bit longer with token ID to look something like `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The `st` is shortcut for "session type" and `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The `tt` is shortcut for "token type" and `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The `gt` is shortcut for grant type and `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

But assuming that every "type" has always 2 characters long shortcut, I've rather updated it in the 2nd commit to have only 7 new characters instead of 18 characters. I planned to squash before merge (unless you think that we should rather use longer format for some reason, in which case the 2nd commit can be removed from the PR).

raw_findings.body: The client session has no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute, so the encoder emits an `na` grant shortcut instead of `cc`; consumers parsing the access-token ID cannot identify it as a client-credentials token.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime token-context decoding returns UNKNOWN for valid client-credentials tokens.
raw_findings.impact: The client session has no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute, so the encoder emits an `na` grant shortcut instead of `cc`; consumers parsing the access-token ID cannot identify it as a client-credentials token.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch makes every access-token ID depend on a grant-type client-session attribute but does not populate that attribute on the direct client-credentials issuance path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to OAuth2Constants.CLIENT_CREDENTIALS in ClientCredentialsGrantType before generating the access token, or centralize this initialization in the shared token-generation path.
raw_findings.title: Client-credentials access tokens are encoded with an unknown grant type
raw_findings.trigger: A client uses the client_credentials grant, whose implementation generates the access token directly instead of going through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse().

raw_findings.body: The resulting token ID contains the `na` shortcut rather than the registered `te` shortcut, so downstream endpoints cannot reliably recognize that it came from token exchange.

raw_findings.impact: The resulting token ID contains the `na` shortcut rather than the registered `te` shortcut, so downstream endpoints cannot reliably recognize that it came from token exchange.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE in the common or legacy token-exchange issuance path before calling generateAccessToken().

raw_findings.body: encodeTokenId() inserts the three-character value into the fixed six-character context, while getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires an encoded context length of six and rejects the newly issued token IDs.
raw_findings.evidence: * @return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants. It can be useful for example in the tokens when the amount of characters should be limited and hence using full grant name
raw_findings.failure_mode: Custom grant providers can issue access tokens that the same server cannot decode.
raw_findings.impact: encodeTokenId() inserts the three-character value into the fixed six-character context, while getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires an encoded context length of six and rejects the newly issued token IDs.
raw_findings.root_cause: The public shortcut documentation allows three characters even though the encoding and decoding format allocates exactly two characters for grant shortcuts.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Define the contract as exactly two characters, correct the documentation, and validate shortcut length and uniqueness during factory initialization and dynamic registration.
raw_findings.title: The shortcut contract permits lengths that the token decoder cannot parse
raw_findings.trigger: A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory follows this new documentation and returns a three-character shortcut.

raw_findings.root_cause: A new abstract method was added to an extension interface without preserving compatibility for existing implementations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Provide a backward-compatible default/migration path for factories lacking shortcuts, or introduce the required method through a compatibility-preserving SPI version and reject unsupported providers with a controlled error.

validated_findings.root_cause: The matcher uses the wrong substring bounds and inverts the expected-grant condition.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Extract the grant shortcut from substring(4, 6) and return its equality result combined with the UUID check, rather than returning false when it matches.
validated_findings.title: Access-token event tests never verify the expected grant shortcut
validated_findings.trigger: Any event assertion uses isAccessTokenId() with a valid encoded access-token ID such as `onrtac:<uuid>`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 483 in AssertEvents.java shows: if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false. The logic is inverted - it returns false (no match) when the shortcut DOES equal expected, and continues to return true when it doesn't match. Additionally, substring(3,5) extracts chars at indices 3-4, but the comment says 4th char which would be index 3, and the format is 6 chars total (2+2+2) so grant shortcut at positions 4-5 would be substring(4,6).

validated_findings.body: encodeTokenId() inserts the three-character value into the fixed six-character context, while getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires an encoded context length of six and rejects the newly issued token IDs.
validated_findings.evidence: * @return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants. It can be useful for example in the tokens when the amount of characters should be limited and hence using full grant name
validated_findings.failure_mode: Custom grant providers can issue access tokens that the same server cannot decode.
validated_findings.impact: encodeTokenId() inserts the three-character value into the fixed six-character context, while getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires an encoded context length of six and rejects the newly issued token IDs.
validated_findings.root_cause: The public shortcut documentation allows three characters even though the encoding and decoding format allocates exactly two characters for grant shortcuts.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Define the contract as exactly two characters, correct the documentation, and validate shortcut length and uniqueness during factory initialization and dynamic registration.
validated_findings.title: The shortcut contract permits lengths that the token decoder cannot parse
validated_findings.trigger: A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory follows this new documentation and returns a three-character shortcut.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 30 documentation states '3-letters shortcut' but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 78-81 show the encoding expects exactly 2 characters per component (substring(0,2), substring(2,4), substring(4,6)) totaling 6 chars. The documentation misleads implementers to use 3-char shortcuts which would break the fixed-width encoding/decoding.

validated_findings.body: The provider fails to compile or throws NoSuchMethodError at runtime, preventing that grant from processing requests.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Provider compatibility is broken for custom grant implementations.
validated_findings.impact: The provider fails to compile or throws NoSuchMethodError at runtime, preventing that grant from processing requests.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch deletes an existing public constructor instead of retaining it and updating it for grantType.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the public copy constructor and copy the new grantType field, or provide an explicit compatibility replacement before removing the constructor.
validated_findings.title: Removing the public Context copy constructor breaks existing grant providers
validated_findings.trigger: An existing custom OAuth2 grant provider calls the public Context(Context) constructor, either when compiled against the new source or when an already-built provider is deployed after upgrade.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows the Context(Context) copy constructor was removed (LEFT side lines 102-116), but the RIGHT side of OAuth2GrantType.java shows the primary constructor now sets this.grantType at line 102. The search for 'super(context' found no matches, indicating no subclasses were using the copy constructor. Without evidence of external custom providers using this constructor, the breaking change claim is speculative.

validated_findings.body: The factory enumeration invokes getShortcut() and can throw AbstractMethodError, causing provider initialization or server startup to fail.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Upgrading with an older custom grant provider can fail during startup rather than degrading safely.
validated_findings.impact: The factory enumeration invokes getShortcut() and can throw AbstractMethodError, causing provider initialization or server startup to fail.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new abstract method was added to an extension interface without preserving compatibility for existing implementations.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Provide a backward-compatible default/migration path for factories lacking shortcuts, or introduce the required method through a compatibility-preserving SPI version and reject unsupported providers with a controlled error.
validated_findings.title: Adding abstract getShortcut breaks previously deployed OAuth2 grant providers
validated_findings.trigger: A previously deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation does not implement the newly added method and is discovered during provider initialization.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 33 adds abstract method String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface. The repository context shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-77 iterates all OAuth2GrantType factories and calls gtf.getShortcut(). Existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory would throw AbstractMethodError when this code runs during postInit.
